drug_class: EZH2 inhibitor (a type of targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Tazemetostat is used to treat certain types of cancer, specifically a cancer of the lymph nodes called follicular lymphoma and a rare cancer of soft tissues called epithelioid sarcoma. It is used in adults whose cancer has come back or has not responded to other treatments. Your doctor chose this medicine because your cancer has specific characteristics that make it a good target for this drug.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have a faulty protein called EZH2 that helps them grow out of control. Tazemetostat works by blocking that faulty protein, which slows down or stops the cancer cells from multiplying. Think of it like putting a lock on the switch that the cancer cells need to keep growing.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include feeling tired or weak, nausea, muscle or joint pain, decreased appetite, vomiting, constipation, diarrhea, and low blood cell counts. Most people tolerate this medication reasonably well, but let your doctor know if any side effects bother you.
warnings: This medication can increase the risk of developing new cancers, including certain blood cancers and serious muscle tumors, so regular monitoring is very important. It can also harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is necessary during treatment and for some time after. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interfere with how tazemetostat works in your body.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 800 mg (four 200 mg tablets) taken by mouth twice a day, every day. Take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time — do not double up.
